draft.title: What the conversation reveals
card: A comparative essay does more than list likenesses and differences. The ending should explain what reading the two texts together shows.
This is a new understanding. It is an idea about a value, an experience or a concern that neither text shows fully on its own.
To write it, ask: what does the second text bring out in the first, or the first in the second? Then state that insight in your own words, tied to the module's focus.
A weak ending only repeats the points already made, or says that the texts are similar and different.
draft.remember: End by saying what the pairing shows that one text alone would not.

a.q: What should the final part of a comparative essay do?
opts: Explain what reading the texts together shows
Restate each text's main technique in turn
List the likenesses and differences once more
Say which of the two texts is the better one
a.why: The ending should give an understanding that comes from reading the texts side by side. Repeating earlier points is tempting, but it adds no new insight.
a.clue: Look for the option that adds something new.

b.q: Ravi compares two texts about migration. Which concluding sentence best shows what the conversation reveals?
opts: Together, the texts show belonging grows through memory too
Both texts use symbols, but the second has more than the first
In conclusion, the texts are alike in some ways and not others
The first text is set in the past and the second is set now
b.why: The first option gives an idea about belonging that comes from putting the two texts together. The second compares techniques, but it does not say what the pairing shows about human experience.
b.clue: Which sentence gives an idea, not just a comparison?
